subject: psychology
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the Edexcel spec.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for GCSE Edexcel Psychology simply, with an example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: What is 'obedience'?
options: Failing to help someone in an emergency
Following a direct order from an authority figure
Changing behaviour due to group pressure from peers
Losing personal identity in a crowd
questions.explain: Obedience is following a direct order from a person perceived to have authority, unlike conformity which is about group pressure from peers.

questions.q: What is 'deindividuation'?
options: A loss of personal identity and responsibility, often in a crowd
Conforming to be liked by a group
questions.explain: Deindividuation is a loss of personal identity and sense of responsibility, often experienced when a person is part of a large crowd.

questions.q: The Edexcel spec divides factors affecting bystander intervention into which two categories?
questions.explain: Factors affecting bystander intervention are classified as personal factors (e.g. empathy) and situational factors (e.g. number of bystanders).

questions.q: A person in a large crowd assumes someone else will help an injured stranger, so does nothing. Which situational factor explains this?
questions.explain: Diffusion of responsibility is a situational factor: as the number of bystanders rises, each person feels less personal responsibility to help.

questions.q: What does 'conformity to majority influence' mean?
options: Changing behaviour or views due to real or imagined group pressure
questions.explain: Conformity to majority influence is changing one's behaviour or opinions because of real or imagined pressure from the larger group.

questions.q: A student privately disagrees with the group's answer but says it aloud to fit in and be accepted. Which type of influence is this?
questions.explain: Publicly agreeing to be accepted while privately disagreeing is normative social influence (compliance), driven by the desire to be liked.

questions.q: The Edexcel spec groups factors affecting conformity to majority influence under which two headings?
questions.explain: Edexcel requires factors affecting conformity to be understood in terms of personality (e.g. locus of control) and the situation (e.g. group size).

questions.q: Asch found that when one confederate broke the group's unanimity by giving the correct answer, conformity fell sharply. This shows the situational factor of:
questions.explain: Breaking the group's unanimity by having an ally give the correct answer greatly reduces conformity, showing the importance of unanimity.

questions.q: Which personality factor makes a person less likely to conform to a majority?
questions.explain: People with an internal locus of control feel they control their own outcomes and are generally less likely to conform to group pressure.

questions.q: The Edexcel spec groups factors affecting obedience under which two headings?
questions.explain: Factors affecting obedience to authority are understood in terms of personality (e.g. authoritarian personality) and the situation (e.g. proximity, uniform).

questions.q: Milgram's agency theory says obedience occurs when a person moves into which state?
questions.explain: In agency theory, obedience happens when a person enters the agentic state, acting as an agent for an authority figure and giving up personal responsibility.

questions.q: French and Raven's social power theory proposes how many 'bases of power' that legitimise an authority figure?
questions.explain: French and Raven (1959) proposed five bases of power: legitimate, reward, expert, referent and coercive power.

questions.q: People obey a person wearing a security uniform more than one in ordinary clothes. This is best explained by which situational factor?
questions.explain: A uniform increases the perceived legitimacy of the authority figure, a situational factor that raises obedience.

questions.q: Adorno et al. (1950) linked a person's likelihood of obeying orders to which personality type?
questions.explain: Adorno et al. proposed that people with an authoritarian personality are more likely to obey orders from authority figures.

questions.q: Which of these is a way suggested to help prevent blind obedience to authority?
options: Educating people about the dangers of blind obedience
questions.explain: Educating people about the dangers of blind obedience and encouraging them to question authority are ways to reduce it, linked to reactance.

questions.q: The Edexcel spec says crowd (collective) behaviour and deindividuation can lead to which outcomes?
questions.explain: Deindividuation in crowds can produce both anti-social behaviour (e.g. football violence) and pro-social behaviour (e.g. a peaceful vigil).

questions.q: In Piliavin et al.'s (1969) subway study, bystanders helped which victim faster and more often?
questions.explain: The 'ill' victim with a cane received help faster and more often than the 'drunk' victim, because the perceived cost of helping was lower.

questions.q: Piliavin et al. (1969) is often praised for high ecological validity. Why?
options: It used a single case study
It was a field experiment on a real subway with real passengers
questions.explain: It was a field experiment carried out on a real New York subway with genuine passengers, giving it high ecological validity.

questions.q: Why was Haney, Banks and Zimbardo's (1973) simulated prison study ended after six days instead of two weeks?
options: Several prisoners showed extreme emotional distress
questions.explain: The study was stopped early because several prisoners suffered extreme emotional reactions and guard behaviour became increasingly hostile.

questions.q: Research suggests people in collectivist cultures may conform more than those in individualist cultures. This is an example of:
options: A social and cultural issue in psychology
questions.explain: Cultural variation in conformity and obedience is a social and cultural issue in psychology, showing that social influence can differ across cultures.
